lines.text: MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is an open standard|for plugging outside systems into an agent as tools.
lines.say: M C P, the Model Context Protocol, is an open standard for plugging outside systems into an agent as tools.

lines.text: A browser, a database, your docs, a search engine.
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and many others support it.
The agent talks to an MCP server, and the server talks to the system.
lines.say: The agent talks to an M C P server, and the server talks to the system.

lines.text: Servers run on your machine, or remotely over HTTP.
lines.say: Servers run on your machine, or remotely over H T T P.

lines.text: At the start, only tool names load.|Full definitions load when a tool is needed, so adding servers barely touches your context.
Servers have scopes too:|local first, then the project's .mcp.json, then your user config.
lines.say: Servers have scopes too: local first, then the project's dot M C P dot JSON, then your user config.

lines.text: These clips were fact-checked with a web search and scraping server.
It searched and fetched the official docs,|and the agent compared the wording before a line was written.
Every claim traces back to an official page,|and each clip lists its sources on screen.
Without it, the agent works from what it remembers, which can be out of date.
Each server is a new set of permissions, so add only what you trust.
Big tool results land in your context, and they count against it.
Pair a server with a skill:|the server gives access, the skill gives the know-how.
Codex configures servers under mcp_servers in config.toml,|and the same servers work in both.
lines.say: Codex configures servers under M C P servers in config dot toml, and the same servers work in both.
